name: West Virginia

stateRatePct.note: The DMV describes a 6% titling sales tax on vehicles with a net purchase price of $500 or more. Under $500 the page lists a flat $30.

tradeInReducesBase.note: The tax is figured on the net purchase price, which is the purchase price minus the trade-in value. The state's new-resident page says the trade-in must first have been titled in West Virginia. Manufacturer rebates are fully taxable and cannot be subtracted.

local.note: The DMV pages describe one statewide titling tax and no local tax.

outOfStateCredit.note: The DMV pages do not say whether tax paid to another state is credited.

amount.note: A two-year registration costs twice the one-year fee. Renewing with a new plate costs the same listed price.

content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} tax when you title a vehicle, figured on the price after your trade-in. There is no local sales tax at titling, and the title and registration fees are modest.

howItWorks.text: The titling tax is {stateRate} of the net purchase price, which is the price minus your trade-in. A manufacturer rebate is fully taxable and cannot be subtracted.
Registration is paid every year, or for two years at twice the yearly fee. Electric and alternative fuel vehicles add a yearly fee on top.
People moving into the state do not pay the titling tax on a vehicle already titled in their name in another state.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the titling tax in West Virginia?
faq.text: Yes. The tax is figured on the purchase price minus the trade-in value. The state's new-resident page notes the trade-in must first have been titled in West Virginia.
Yes. The DMV says manufacturer rebates are fully taxable and cannot be subtracted from the purchase price.

faq.q: Do electric vehicles pay more to register?
faq.text: Yes. Electric and alternative fuel vehicles add a yearly fee to the registration fee. Hybrids add a separate smaller fee.
